question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int 9\cos\left(2 - 6 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=2 - 6 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(- \frac{1}{6}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9\cos\left(2 - 6 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=9\left(- \frac{1}{6}\right)\int \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{3}{2}\int \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{3}{2}\left(\sin\left(u\right)\right)+C\\ &=- \frac{3}{2}\sin\left(2 - 6 x\right)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{7}} 3\cos\left(7 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=7 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=7,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=7\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)=0\\ x=\frac{\pi}{7}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=7\left(\frac{\pi}{7}\right)+\left(0\right)=\pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{7}} 3\cos\left(7 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=3\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)\int_{0}^{\pi} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{3}{7}\int_{0}^{\pi} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{3}{7}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{0}^{\pi}\\ &=\frac{3}{7}\left(\sin\left(\pi\right)-\sin\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{3}{7}\left(\left(0\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=0.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\pi}{9}}^{- \frac{\pi}{18}} 6\cos\left(6 x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=6 x + \frac{\pi}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(- \frac{\pi}{9}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=- \frac{\pi}{6}\\ x=- \frac{\pi}{18}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(- \frac{\pi}{18}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{- \frac{\pi}{9}}^{- \frac{\pi}{18}} 6\cos\left(6 x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=6\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\int_{- \frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\int_{- \frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{- \frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\\ &=1\left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\sin\left(- \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=1\left(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\pi}{15}}^{\frac{\pi}{15}} \cos\left(- \frac{5 x}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=- \frac{5 x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=- \frac{5}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(- \frac{2}{5}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{15}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=- \frac{5}{2}\left(- \frac{\pi}{15}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{15}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=- \frac{5}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{15}\right)+\left(0\right)=- \frac{\pi}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed bounds decrease because the inner derivative is negative. Keep their order together with the negative substitution factor.

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{- \frac{\pi}{15}}^{\frac{\pi}{15}} \cos\left(- \frac{5 x}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=1\left(- \frac{2}{5}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{- \frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{2}{5}\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{- \frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{2}{5}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{- \frac{\pi}{6}}\\ &=- \frac{2}{5}\left(\sin\left(- \frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{2}{5}\left(\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\pi}{5}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \frac{5}{4}\sin\left(- \frac{5 x}{2} + \frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=- \frac{5 x}{2} + \frac{2 \pi}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=- \frac{5}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(- \frac{2}{5}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{5}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=- \frac{5}{2}\left(- \frac{\pi}{5}\right)+\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)=\frac{7 \pi}{6}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{6}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=- \frac{5}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed bounds decrease because the inner derivative is negative. Keep their order together with the negative substitution factor.

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{- \frac{\pi}{5}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \frac{5}{4}\sin\left(- \frac{5 x}{2} + \frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=\frac{5}{4}\left(- \frac{2}{5}\right)\int_{\frac{7 \pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{1}{2}\int_{\frac{7 \pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{1}{2}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{7 \pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-\cos\left(\frac{7 \pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left(\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{7 \pi}{8}}^{\frac{15 \pi}{16}} \frac{5}{3}\cos\left(\frac{4 x}{3} + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{4 x}{3} + \frac{\pi}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{4}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{7 \pi}{8}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{7 \pi}{8}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{5 \pi}{3}\\ x=\frac{15 \pi}{16}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{15 \pi}{16}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{7 \pi}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{\frac{7 \pi}{8}}^{\frac{15 \pi}{16}} \frac{5}{3}\cos\left(\frac{4 x}{3} + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=\frac{5}{3}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\int_{\frac{5 \pi}{3}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{4}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{5}{4}\int_{\frac{5 \pi}{3}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{4}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{5}{4}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{5 \pi}{3}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{4}}\\ &=\frac{5}{4}\left(\sin\left(\frac{7 \pi}{4}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{5}{4}\left(\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{8} + \frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
